idea: Heritage and listed building retrofit advisory for owners
buyer: Owners of listed and heritage commercial buildings
pain: Retrofit obligations collide with heritage constraints and nobody can price the conflict
v1: A retrofit options study for one listed building
verdict: A genuinely hard problem she is well suited to, but heritage specialists already hold this ground.

why.distribution: One hop through architecture and property contacts.
why.demand: Owners face real compliance pressure and do pay specialists.
why.fmf: Architecture plus cost modelling fits well; heritage conservation is a specialism she lacks.
why.defensibility: Conservation accreditation matters here and she does not have it.
why.tailwind: Retrofit obligations are tightening across the whole building stock.
why.ceiling: £9k x 22 buildings = £198k, requiring volume she cannot reach without accreditation.

ceiling_arithmetic: £9k x 22 buildings = £198k. Without conservation accreditation she competes at the margins. Realistic: 5-7 = £45-63k.
carries: A real and tightening regulatory driver on a genuinely difficult technical problem.
kills: Accreditation. Heritage work is gatekept by conservation credentials she would need years to obtain.
test: Ask two heritage building owners who advises them on retrofit.
test_pass: They describe a gap between the conservation architect and the finance team.
test_fail: They name an accredited conservation practice.
